pyqgis_plugin.name: Quick Find
pyqgis_plugin.description: Toolbar search box: type any value (e.g. MIN164) or a latitude, longitude, press Enter, and the map zooms to the matching feature or drops a temporary pin.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Searches every text field (and numeric fields for numbers) of the visible vector layers. Exact matches come first, then whole-word matches (MIN164 inside MIN_R3R3_ANL6_MIN164), then partial ones (MIN1640) only when nothing better exists. Press Enter again for the next match; the arrow button lists all matches and the options. Cmd+F (Mac) or Ctrl+F (Windows) jumps to the box and back to the map; Esc also returns to the map. While loaded, Quick Find takes that key from Layer > Filter… (still available in the Layer menu) and gives it back when unloaded. Type or paste a latitude, longitude (decimal like 7.119291, 125.6281, degrees-minutes-seconds like 7°07'09.4"N 125°37'41.2"E, or a Google Maps link) to zoom there and drop a temporary pin with the coordinates; the pin is not a layer and goes away when you clear the box or search again (or Remove pin in the menu). The Capture lat/long button lets you click the map to drop the pin there and copies its coordinates. From the ▾ menu, Add pin to layer saves the pin as a point in any point layer, filling Latitude/Longitude (or lat/long, x/y) fields and asking for a name when the layer has a name field; the layer is left in edit mode so you save or roll back the edit. The Street View button (or Open in Street View in the ▾ menu) opens Google Street View at the pin in your browser; only the pin coordinates are sent, and only when you click it. Attribute searches never edit layers. My location drops a pin where the computer is: Windows Location on Windows; on a Mac a Shortcuts-app shortcut (set up once, steps shown). Save pin keeps any pin (search, capture or my location) in a 'Saved pins' GeoPackage layer: a small Save window asks for name, remarks, colour and marker size (colour and size default to your last choice), and each pin is drawn as a Google-Earth-style pushpin in its own colour and size (Route Drawer's KMZ export uses Google Earth's own pushpin, tinted and scaled the same). Pins are saved into the group selected in the Layers panel (the selected group, or the group of the selected layer; the top level otherwise): each group keeps its own Saved pins layer and file (e.g. saved_pins_sub-group1.gpkg), made only when you press Save, and the Save window says where the pin goes. The Layers panel shows one entry per colour used, labelled with the pins in it (updated after each save or edit). If the top-level Saved pins layer was taken off the map, the next save starts a new dated file and says where the previous one is kept; ⚙ menu > Keep saved pins in… opens a file again, in the selected group. The point layer last used for Add pin to layer is remembered between sessions. Filter layers (funnel button) opens a panel to show only the features with a chosen value in a chosen column, e.g. one AN_Loop_Name, on the chosen layer and every other layer with that column; step through values with the arrows, optionally label and colour by a column; Clear restores each layer's own filter and style. Fast on big projects: each layer's names and IDs are read once and kept in memory (refreshed when the layer changes), layers over 200,000 features such as a whole-country roads layer are skipped unless you turn on 'Search large layers too', and the slower search of remarks/descriptions runs by itself only on small layers (otherwise a Search all fields button is offered). Works on QGIS 3.22+ (Qt5) and QGIS 4 (Qt6), on Windows and Mac.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Route Drawer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Draw a polyline or route on the map by clicking points (along the roads if you like); import CSV pins and KMZ with all their data, export layers to KMZ or Excel, and click features to see their data and open their links.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Click Draw Route, then click points on the map. With Follow Roads on, each new click connects to the previous one along the shortest path on your road layer (auto-picked by name, e.g. gis_osm_roads_free_1; change it from the options button); Shift+click draws a straight segment. Hold the left button (or drag) to draw freehand: points follow the cursor until you release, and one right-click removes the whole stroke. Arrow keys or W/A/S/D move the map a quarter view while drawing, even mid-stroke. Right-click (or Backspace) undoes the last point, Esc cancels, press Enter to save. While drawing, a label beside the cursor shows the total length and the distance to the cursor in metres (ellipsoidal), also shown in the status bar; saved routes are labelled with their length in metres (toggle in the options menu). Saving opens a small Save window: name, remarks, colour and line width (colour and width default to your last choice); each route is drawn in its own colour and width and keeps them in KMZ export; remarks become the placemark description (balloon text), and pins export as Google Earth pushpins in their own colour and size. Routes are saved into the group selected in the Layers panel (the selected group, or the group of the selected layer; the top level otherwise): each group keeps its own Drawn routes layer and file (e.g. drawn_routes_sub-group1.gpkg), made only when you press Save, and the Save window says where the route goes. The Layers panel shows one entry per colour used, labelled with the routes in it (updated after each save or edit). If the top-level Drawn routes layer was taken off the map, the next save starts a new dated file and says where the previous one is kept; options button > Save routes in… opens a file again, in the selected group. Routes are saved with name, length_m, method, created, remarks, color and width_mm fields to a "Drawn routes" GeoPackage layer (~/Documents/QGIS Drawn Routes/drawn_routes.gpkg by default), or into the selected line layer when it is in edit mode. The Import/Export button imports a CSV as pins (latitude/longitude columns found automatically, also degrees-minutes-seconds, decimal commas and one combined column) and a KMZ/KML with all ExtendedData, folders and colours (read piece by piece, so even very large KMZ files work), and exports what is highlighted in the Layers panel (one layer, several layers, or a whole group such as pins + lines: one KMZ folder or Excel sheet per layer) to a standard KMZ (map colours, names, descriptions, all attributes, folders) or to Excel (all attributes plus coordinates, lengths or areas). Pins in boundary (toolbar button) opens a panel: choose a region, province, town/city or barangay (NAMRIA/PSA boundaries from HDX, read straight from the downloaded zip; OpenStreetMap admin areas as a fallback), a polygon of any layer, or draw your own (kept in My boundaries for next time), one or several at once; Select pins selects the pins inside in the ticked point layers (a pin on the line counts as inside), and Extract copies them to a new layer, KMZ and/or Excel, each pin with a 'boundary' column naming the boundary it is in. The Info tool shows all data of a clicked feature; links such as GDrive open in the browser. The chosen road layer is remembered between sessions by its file: next time it is found again in the project, or, if it is not loaded, its file is used in the background without adding it to the map. The import folder is remembered too. Respects the project's snapping settings. The road layer is only read. Works on QGIS 3.22+ (Qt5) and QGIS 4 (Qt6), on Windows and Mac.
